question.problem:
$$
⟨f(x),g(x)⟩={\int }_{-\pi }^{\pi }f(x)g(x)\,\text{d}x
$$

Given the inner product on the set of continuous functions over $x\in [-\pi ,\pi )$ defined above, select the correct options below.

$\,$
$⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡(4x),\operatorname{sin}⁡(7x)⟩=$
{{field-1}}

$\,$
The functions $f(x)=\operatorname{sin}⁡(4x)$ and $g(x)=\operatorname{sin}⁡(7x)$ 
{{field-2}}.
question.worked_solution:
We begin by using the product-to-sum identity

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡(4x)\operatorname{sin}⁡(7x)=\frac{1}{2}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)-\operatorname{cos}⁡(11x)).
$$

Substituting this into the integral gives

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡(4x),\operatorname{sin}⁡(7x)⟩ & ={\int }_{-\pi }^{\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡(4x)\operatorname{sin}⁡(7x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-\pi }^{\pi }\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(11x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[\frac{1}{6}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)-\frac{1}{22}\operatorname{sin}⁡(11x)]}_{-\pi }^{\pi } \\  & =\frac{1}{6}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(3\pi )-\operatorname{sin}⁡(-3\pi ))-\frac{1}{22}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(11\pi )-\operatorname{sin}⁡(-11\pi )) \\  & =\frac{1}{6}(0-0)-\frac{1}{22}(0-0) \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $f(x)=\operatorname{sin}⁡(4x)$ and $g(x)=\operatorname{sin}⁡(7x)$ 
$\text{are orthogonal}$ with respect to the inner product.
